The student reviews and may amend them before the first run; any change after the first run is recorded as a post-hoc disagreement, not silently applied.
annotator: Drafted by Claude; approval by the student pending at the time of this commit
selectionRules: Each case has exactly two eligible shelters after the hard constraints; no near-tie is intended; the stated need decides the answer. SYN-16 is a control that every method should get right.

SYN-09.rationale: A bleeding animal that cannot stand needs a vet immediately. Only B has one on site; A can merely arrange one. 3 km more travel is worth it.

SYN-10.rationale: Both have a vet. A is 1.7 km closer but has a 90-minute intake wait; B takes the animal in 20 minutes. Time to treatment is shorter at B.

SYN-11.rationale: The dog is near a road, so reaching it fast matters most. A is 4.5 km nearer and has 2 slots, which is enough for one animal. Extra capacity at B is not needed.

SYN-12.tests: proximity and immediate intake versus capacity
SYN-12.rationale: Highway danger. A is 1 km away with intake in 10 minutes; one slot is enough. B is farther and slower.

SYN-13.rationale: The animal is safe and will stay a while. A shelter that does not take rabbits cannot house it properly, however near. B accepts rabbits.

SYN-14.tests: capacity for a longer stay versus proximity
SYN-14.rationale: No urgency. A has one slot left; B has room, and a short extra distance matters little for a safe animal.

SYN-15.tests: data freshness and confidence versus proximity
SYN-15.rationale: A's capacity figures are stale and low-confidence, so its 4 slots may not exist. B's are live and high-confidence for 0.8 km more.

SYN-16.rationale: Identical shelters except distance (2 km versus 12 km): the nearer one is better under any sensible method. If a method fails this, the method is broken.
